newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends firm after turnaround.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends firm after turnaround.

text.p: Spring wheat futures ended firm and above their intraday lows in a light-volume recovery that driven by commercial and fund buying, traders said.
"We had a surprising rebound in here," a MGE floor source said.
Spring wheat dropped early on spillover pressure from CBOT corn and soybeans, which weakened after much-needed rains fell in dry growing areas of west-central Illinois.
MGE September spring wheat opened down three cents per bushel and proceeded to hit an intraday low at $3.69, down 10-1/4 cents on the day.

But spring wheat firmed at midsession as Cargill Investor Services stepped in and bought around 700,000 Sept bushels. Further strength came as funds bought wheat in Chicago, Kansas City and Minneapolis.
MGE spring wheat settled one to eight cents higher, with new crop September up four cents at $3.83-1/4.
Traders said dealings were active early but slowed at midsession. The MGE estimated Monday's volume at 13.375 million bushels, down sharply from 23.515 million Friday.
Apart from Cargill, other featured players included Country Hedging, which bought 800,000 Sept bushels. Benson-Quinn sold 800,000 Sept.
